findings.evidence: "Verification codes are 6 digits long, and this one has 5. Check the message again and enter all six."
findings.fix: Simplify to "Enter all six digits" or "This code needs 6 digits. Please enter the complete code."
findings.location: Two-factor setup, verification code - first message
findings.violation: The message uses "all six" when the context already established "6 digits", creating redundancy without clarifying what action the user should take with the entered code.

findings.evidence: "This verification code expired 10 minutes after it was sent, which stops an intercepted code from being reused later."
findings.fix: Shorten the message to "This verification code expired. Request a new code and enter it here." Keep the technical detail out of the error message.
findings.location: Two-factor setup, verification code - second message
findings.violation: The explanation of why codes expire is lengthy and technical for a user who just needs to fix their immediate problem; it may confuse users who do not care about security rationale.

findings.fix: Include the year: "This promo code ended on 30 June 2024" or use relative phrasing: "This promo code expired."
findings.violation: The date is written as "30 June" without a year, making it unclear whether the code expired this year, last year, or in a future year from the user's perspective.

findings.evidence: "This promo code applies to annual plans, and the selected plan is monthly. Change the plan to annual, or remove the code."
findings.fix: Reorder or clarify priorities: "This code only works with annual plans. Switch to an annual plan to use it, or enter a different code."
findings.violation: The message presents two unequal options (changing plan or removing code) without clarifying which is the recommended path or the impact of each choice.
